question: The resistance of a wire of length L and area of cross-section A is 1.0 Ω. The resistance of a wire of the same material, but of length 4 L and area of cross-section 5 A will be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.8 Ω.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **resistance of a wire** is** directly proportional** to its** length** and **inversely proportional **to its** area of cross-section.**
 
• Using the formula **R = Ω (L/A), **where Ω is the** resistivity **of the material, we can find the resistance of the second wire.
 
• Since the material is the same, the resistivity **remains constant.**
 
• Therefore, R2 = 1.0 Ω (4L/5A) = 4/5(L/A) = 4/5(R1) =** 0.8 Ω.**
 
• Hence,** 0.8 Ω** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The amount of** obstruction to current passage** in an electrical circuit is measured as **resistance.**
 
• **Ohms**, a unit of measurement for resistance, are represented by the** Greek letter omega (Ω).**
 
• The** electric current **flowing through a conductor between two places is** directly proportional** to the** voltage across** those same points, according to **Ohm's law.**
